questions.prompt: What is the strongest evidence that an application design is ready for review?
options: Only a screenshot of the happy path.
A successful compile with no runtime checks or acceptance criteria.
Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
A large number of abstractions without tests.
questions.answer_key: Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.explanation: Production-oriented work is supported by explicit acceptance criteria and repeatable evidence.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Scalable Project Structure”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with feature-oriented organization and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with feature-oriented organization and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Feature-oriented organization”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Scalable Project Structure”?
options: Check shared libraries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume avoiding circular dependencies and overly broad modules is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check shared libraries, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Shared libraries”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
